description.plain:
Coldplay is a British rock band, formed in 1997 by University College London classmates Chris Martin (vocals, guitar, piano), Jonny Buckland (guitar) and Guy Berryman (bass), along with drummer Will Champion. The band’s name comes from Tim Crompton, a student who was in the same university as the members (University College London) at the time.

Once they issued their debut, Parachutes in 2000, many saw them as a Radiohead knock-off. No doubt, Coldplay’s sound —elegant, melodic, vaguely spacey and very dramatic — bore plenty of similarity to mid-1990s Radiohead. But the group’s hooks, sharpened by frontman Chris Martin’s ability to pull heartstrings, and the their willingness to evolve their sound, gave Coldplay staying power. The greatest examples are second album A Rush of Blood to the Head (2002), which was generally considered to be musically and lyrically more mature and sophisticated, and less obviously the product of one particular influence, and the fourth one Viva La Vida or Death and All His Friends (2008), where producer Brian Eno influenced the band to broaden their sound and led to various sonic landscapes. Both won the Grammy Award for Best Rock Album and spawned sucessful singles such as “Clocks”, “Viva la Vida”, “In My Place”, “Violet Hill” and “The Scientist”.

As a result, the band became one of the most commercially successful acts of the new millennium, with over 80 million albums sold – even if along with the acclaim came a vocal opposition, due to the supposedly derivative nature, the overtly emotional lyrics, and the fact they’re good-mannered English boys instead of wild rockstars. As a result, Coldplay are thought as either a punchline showing all that’s wrong with 21st century rock, or a really good if overplayed band with songs tailor made for stadium performances.

description.plain:
“The Scientist” is a very mellow song about trying to analyze a broken relationship.

The song’s melody is inspired by “Don’t Look Back in Anger” by the Oasis, especially the piano part.

The music video is famous for its reverse chronology (which required Chris Martin to learn the song backwards in order to make it look like he was singing forwards as he walked backwards…).  Although the video fits the song well, the idea for the video came to Director Jamie Thraves independently; he then waited for the perfect song to match his concept.

description.plain:
Revered as an essential rock song of the 2000s, “Viva la Vida” tells the story of a monarch who’s lost his kingdom. In another aspect, the song is also seen as a narrative on the French Revolution given the historical and biblical references in the lyrics. The instrumental is based around a string and piano background, led by an orchestral drum beat.

The title derives from the Spanish phrase “Long Live Life,” and takes its name from Frida Kahlo’s last painting before her death. During a March 2008 interview with Rolling Stone, frontman Chris Martin explained the reason for naming the song and album in honor of Kahlo:

She went through a lot of s–t, of course, and then she started a big painting in her house that said ‘Viva la Vida.’ I loved the boldness of it. […] It just felt right.

This song debuted to massive success and acclaim, peaking at number one on both the Billboard 100 and UK Singles Chart. Coldplay received several awards for the track, including Song of the Year at the Grammy Awards in February 2009.

The chorus has musical similarities to Joe Satriani’s instrumental piece, “If I Could Fly.” Satriani sued Coldplay for plagiarism—they settled out of court. The band Creaky Boards also accused Coldplay of taking the song’s melody from their record, “The Songs I Didn’t Write,” however, Coldplay denied the allegations.

Coldplay released two music videos for this song. Hype Williams made the official video, which premiered in August 2008, depicting the band against a backdrop of Eugène Delacroix’s painting, Liberty Leading the People. The alternate music video dropped alongside the first one but was directed by Anton Corbijn and starred Chris Martin as a king.

description.plain:
“Fix You” is the fourth track and second single from Coldplay’s third album X&Y. It was written by Chris Martin for his then-wife, Gwyneth Paltrow, to comfort her after her father passed away.

The song was covered memorably with an unexpectedly moving rendition by the Young@Heart chorus, a choir made up entirely of elderly singers. This event was captured by the award-winning 2006 documentary film about the group, Young@Heart.

https://youtu.be/G-e8LGMPTtE
On 20 May 2020 a cover by English singer Sam Smith was broadcast on iHeart Radio. Sam said “I love this song, and …  was just reminded again of how much of a classic it is”.  On 6th July Sam’s version was released to the acclaim of their fans. Sam wrote on social media “Thank you @coldplay for writing such a beautiful song”. The simplest praise is the most meaningful.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ebB1fvJzT24

description.plain:
“Yellow” is the fifth track and second single off of Coldplay’s 2000 debut album Parachutes. It is their oldest and its most enduring hit, continuing to be a celebrated staple of live performances even today. The title of the song came from the feel of the band during its composition, which was described as filled with “brightness and hope and devotion”. However, the lyrical content was inspired by lead singer Chris Martin’s “unrequited love”.

(Source: Coldplay: Nobody Said It Was Easy by Martin Roach)

description.plain:
Coldplay’s Queen B duet is an ode to enjoying a significant other you love and cherish. In an interview, Martin described the origins of the collaboration and its sound:

I thought I’d like to have a song called “Drinks on Me” where you sit on the side of a club and buy everyone drinks because you’re so fucking cool. I was chuckling about that, when this melody came – “drinks on me, drinks on me” – then the rest of the song came out. I presented it to the rest of the band and they said, “We love this song, but there’s no way you can sing ‘drinks on me.’” So that changed into “drink from me” and the idea of having an angelic person in your life. Then that turned into asking Beyonce to sing on it.

It’s one of four collaborations on the album; the others are Tove Lo on “Fun”, Gwyneth Paltrow on “Everglow”, and a Barack Obama sample on “Kaleidoscope.”

Apparently, Beyonce also made their album 90% better.

She made our album 90% better. And we were already 20% good. So now we’re like 110% the band we used to be. You do the math.

Before the album’s December 4, 2015 release date, it was previewed on Twitter on November 24, 2015. The official music video was uploaded on the 29th of January.

body.plain:
Coldplay’s Queen B duet is an ode to enjoying a significant other you love and cherish. In an interview, Martin described the origins of the collaboration and its sound:

I thought I’d like to have a song called “Drinks on Me” where you sit on the side of a club and buy everyone drinks because you’re so fucking cool. I was chuckling about that, when this melody came – “drinks on me, drinks on me” – then the rest of the song came out. I presented it to the rest of the band and they said, “We love this song, but there’s no way you can sing ‘drinks on me.’” So that changed into “drink from me” and the idea of having an angelic person in your life. Then that turned into asking Beyonce to sing on it.

It’s one of four collaborations on the album; the others are Tove Lo on “Fun”, Gwyneth Paltrow on “Everglow”, and a Barack Obama sample on “Kaleidoscope.”

Apparently, Beyonce also made their album 90% better.

She made our album 90% better. And we were already 20% good. So now we’re like 110% the band we used to be. You do the math.

Before the album’s December 4, 2015 release date, it was previewed on Twitter on November 24, 2015. The official music video was uploaded on the 29th of January.

description.plain:
One of Coldplay’s most hyped tracks ever, described by attendees of Coldplay’s secret Ghost Stories shows as “wonderfully produced” and “upbeat, happy, makes you want to stand up and dance”, “A Sky Full of Stars” is the centerpiece of Ghost Stories, bringing the emotional treadmill to an explosive climax.

The track was released as Coldplay’s second single from Ghost Stories, after “Magic”, with the track premiering on 29 April 2014.

EDM artist Avicii was a primary producer on the track and Chris Martin later revealed in an interview that he asked the producer to play the piano parts.

description.plain:
The most personal and emotionally-charged song on Coldplay’s enigmatic A Head Full of Dreams, “Everglow” expresses memory and loss as an ever-lasting “glow.”

Most likely inspired by his own divorce from actress Gwyneth Paltrow, songwriter Chris Martin stated during an interview with Zane Lowe:

To me, [the song] is about — whether it’s a loved one or a situation or a friend or a relationship that’s finished, or someone’s passed away — I was thinking about, after you’ve been through the sadness of something, you also get this everglow. That’s what it’s about.

description.plain:
The groovy fifth track on Coldplay’s dynamic A Head Full of Dreams takes a step into disco, with a simplistic song about life and love, backed by a funky dance floor beat. It features a prominent guitar riff that was inspired by the riff on Guns N' Roses “Sweet Child O' Mine.”

According to bassist Guy Berryman,

[The track] started as a freeform musical session and was called something else, Legends or something. It had a different chord sequence and different hooks and one-by-one things were taken away and things got added.

description.plain:
The third track and lead single off Mylo Xyloto, Coldplay makes a true masterpiece of the song “Paradise”. With its jittery synths, orchestral hooks, thunderous drumming, and falsetto vocals by frontman Chris Martin, this is a win-win for everyone, and critics and fans alike.

The song is about how the real world can be escaped through dreams and paradise. In context of the album’s concept, it shows how the rebel leader Fly is just some shuteye away. The song describes her obstacles in life, and how she first noticed that the government system in Silencia is corrupted, due to Major Minus.

description.plain:
The second track on Coldplay’s sixth studio album Ghost Stories, “Magic”, introduces us to the narrator’s former relationship with a woman he loved in a magical way. Through clever references to the art of stage magic, he describes a very special bond that once existed between the two.

The song is not an affirmation of a relationship, it is a song about honoring yourself when a relationship ends. Although his lover has broken him in two by ending the relationship, he celebrates the magic of his capacity to unconditionally love another, even if they don’t reciprocate — his precious jewel.

“Magic” was the lead single from Coldplay’s Ghost Stories and was released on March 3, 2014.

description.plain:
Continuing the existential themes of A Rush of Blood to the Head, “Clocks” opens with a haunting piano melody into Chris Martin’s falsetto vocals.

The song concerns the paradox facing humanity: an obsession with time and punctuality versus a desire to savor every moment and “seize the day.” The lyrics speak to this universal existential anxiety.

 Several remixes exist of the song, and there are many samples of the piano riff used throughout the song. “Clocks” was well received by critics and even won “Record of the Year” at the 2004 Grammy Awards.

description.plain:
The closing track off Everyday Life showcases a slow piano ballad that describes and summarizes the band’s general album message: love, equality, pain, struggles, legacy, humanity, hope, everyday life.
It follows how everyone is different but we’re all part of the same big family.

The main chord progression, F#m – A – Em – Bm, is the same as that of album opener Church.

description.plain:
In the dramatic and uplifting grand finale of Coldplay’s enigmatic A Head Full of Dreams, the band presents us with a power ballad that encourages belief and optimism in both life and love, through emphasis on hardships and empowering music led by a melancholy piano riff, seemingly inspired by the likes of Train and other big-sound rock bands of the early 2000s.

Touted by Chris Martin as “the song that they’ve been waiting to write for fifteen years”, the song not only represents a beautiful conclusion to A Head Full of Dreams, but also a chapter in the life of Coldplay themselves, with Martin having noted the album as “the completion of something.”

description.plain:
The co-lead single “Arabesque” (which is the lead single for the Sunrise part of the album) is Coldplay’s way of trying to sew peace in the wake of the western fear of Islam with the war on terrorism going on. Instrumentally, the song merges western musical styles with Middle Eastern rhythms (like with the guitar & saxophone) placing the idea that “music unites us all”.

Arabesque is a visual art genre, which was mostly used in Islamic countries. For example, in architecture, it’s an ornamental design consisting of intertwined flowing lines, originally found in ancient Islamic art. While in dance and ballet, it is a dancing posture. The name of the songs is very apropos to the whole theme of the album being Arabic and bringing the culture to western media. The meaning of the track is also parallel and similar to the song “بنی آدم (Son of Adam)” by the Persian poet, Sadi.

description.plain:
“Hypnotised” is a “dreamlike ballad” from the British rock band Coldplay’s 2017 EP, Kaleidoscope. It is the second song from the EP to be announced, and is the fifth track on what will be a five track EP, planned for release on June 2, 2017.

Described as a “non-single” by the group, it was announced on the official Coldplay site on the March 2, 2017, coinciding with lead singer Chris Martin’s 40th birthday, and in anticipation of the EP’s release on June 2. It can be listened to via most of the mainstream music services.

https://twitter.com/coldplay/status/837210972817219584

The track was released alongside what writers described as being “a captivating lyric video” directed by Mary Wigmore. Chris Martin said the following about the release of “Hypnotised:”

“Hypnotised” won’t necessarily be a “single,” as much as it simply the first offering from the EP.

description.plain:
“Fly On” is the first of two songs that appears on the ninth and final track on Coldplay’s sixth studio album, Ghost Stories, entitled “O”. The song, “O”, itself is the ambient piece that comes after “Fly On”, for those who are confused.

Arguably one of the saddest songs written by the band, “Fly On” brings the emotional treadmill to an end, after a 40-minute spiritual journey, encapsulating the narrator’s newly-realized feelings about the woman he once called his own: Like a flock of birds, love comes and goes, and it’s not worth hurting over.

description.plain:
“Violet Hill” is off of Coldplay’s album Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends. It was their first attempt at a protest/political song.

The first line “It was a long and dark December” was actually the first line the band ever wrote, but they could never finish the rest of the song. The rest of the song came about after watching Bill O'Reilly rant, and Chris thinking about a musician friend who worked in a bar and struggled with his boss, leading to lyrics about having your life run by people you don’t like.

description.plain:
The chord progression for “Church"— F#m – A – Em – Bm—bookends the album. It is recalled for the closing track, Everyday Life.

The song draw a thin parallelism between the beauty and heartwarming presence of a girl that makes you feel secure and safe, and a place, the “Church”, in which a strong believer can feel the same emotions of joy and unconditional safeness.

description.plain:
The lead single off Parachutes, “Shiver” (alongside fan favorite “Yellow”) helped establish Coldplay in the new millennium alt-rock scene.

Chris Martin derisively describes it as a “stalking song” in line with the likes of the Police and Jeff Buckley.

According to Martin, the track was written for a specific woman in mind but never disclosed who. Many speculated that it was  Natalie Imbruglia but Martin denies this, stating her only role was visual inspiration.

description.plain:
The opening track on Coldplay’s largely-anticipated sixth studio album, Ghost Stories; a haunting, ambient teardrop follow up to the band’s technicolour rock opera explosion, 2011’s Mylo Xyloto.

The song introduces the basic narrative and the two characters of Ghost Stories; a man, whose point of view is represented in this album, and a woman who he loved very much but had broken away from him.

description.plain:
“Midnight” was teased by Coldplay before it’s release.



It was their first (with the exception of “Atlas” for the Hunger Games soundtrack) release of new material since Mylo Xyloto in 2011. It later appeared on the band’s sixth LP, Ghost Stories.

The song represents a change in style, with Chris Martin’s heavily processed vocals being the focal point which drew comparisons to Bon Iver.

description.plain:
“O”, the titular song on the ninth and final track on Coldplay’s sixth studio album Ghost Stories, brings the journey to a close with a soulful ambient piece with a voice asking, “Don’t ever let go”.

A Western-influenced guitar version of “O”, titled “O (Reprise)”, was released as the final track on the A Sky Full Of Stars EP. This song, along with the other two non-album tracks on the EP (“All Your Friends” and “Ghost Story”), were re-released as part of the Target deluxe edition of Ghost Stories.

description.plain:
The seventh track of the album, “Green Eyes” has a country-rock vibe to it.

Chris Martin wrote the song as a ballad for a former girlfriend who, obviously, had green eyes. When Chris started dating Gwyneth Palthrow in 2002, he decided against performing the song live as it offended her. Instead, he chose to play Moses, a song written for Palthrow.

Later he said the following about the discussion: “It’s not about the right person. It’s like an old pair of trousers, it doesn’t fit.”

description.plain:
Marked by a somber mood, Coldplay’s anthem for Christmas is one that metaphorizes the lights and decorations of the festive season as beacons of warmth and hope for those feeling left in the cold during Christmas. The song follows a first-person perspective of a person mourning the verbally violent breakup of a relationship on Christmas Eve, with the heartening spirit of the holidays to guide him and others to a happier and merrier Christmas, as it should be.

Originally released in December 2010 as a surprise, straight from the recording sessions that would spawn the technicolor marvel known as Mylo Xyloto, “Christmas Lights”, for its festive themes, has been a recurring staple of Christmas celebrations for Coldplay fans each December.

description.plain:
“بنی آدم (Children of Adam)” is a song inspired by the Persian poem of the same name (or sometimes also called “Bani Adam”) by Saadi Shirazi. The poem in English reads:

Humans (Children of Adam) are inherent parts (or more literally, limbs) of one body, and are from the same valuable essence (or more literally, gem) in their creation.
When the conditions of the time hurt one of these parts, other parts will be disturbed.
If you are indifferent about the misery of others,
it may not be appropriate to call you a human being.



The word بنی (bani) is the plural form of ابن (ibn) in Arabic which means son. However, in this poem, the intention of Saadi was the whole humankind and the “Children of Adam” would give a more appropriate meaning to the content.

“Talk” is the third single from Coldplay’s third album, X&Y. It features lyrics about feeling insecure and how conversation could fix it, and  a recurring melodic hook directly inspired by the synth motif prevalent in Kraftwerk’s “Computer Love”.



Commercially, it was a success, reaching number one in Poland and the Netherlands and the top ten in Spain and UK. In the US, it hit the top ten of Alternative and Adult Pop Songs, and topped the Hot Dance Club songs.

description.plain:
God Put A Smile Upon Your Face is the fourth song off of Coldplay’s second studio album, A Rush Of Blood To The Head

The song is basically saying that one should appreciate what they have, because life is short and nobody knows what actually happens after death. If there is a heaven, hell, or moral code––nobody knows.

Despite Coldplay’s massive popularity at the time in the UK (and now), the single only peaked at 100––only promo copies were released. However, it was a top 40 hit in The Netherlands and New Zealand, and hit number three in Poland.

description.plain:
The hidden track of X&Y, “‘Til Kingdom Come” was originally intended to be a collaboration with Johnny Cash, but he died before his part could be recorded – this explains why the song has a very country vibe to it (Rihanna would later have the “honor” of being Coldplay’s first collaboration on an LP).

At its core, “‘Til Kingdom Come” is a ballad about Death coming to claim a man at the end of his life (a fitting theme given that Cash was close to death himself). When played at live performances, the band usually combine the song with Cash’s “Ring of Fire.”

description.plain:
Continuing from Mylo Xyloto, Hurts Like Heaven continues the story of Mylo and Xyloto, and opens up the world to the listener, as well as early life. With 1984 8-bit synths, amazing drumming, refrained bass hooks, distorted and high-hitting guitars, and the best vocals from Chris Martin, the song will rivet you through damnation and back, as it talks about the oppression of government, rebellion, and love, with Silencia turning into a living hell.



Talking through the early points of Mylo Xyloto’s life, his parents were affiliated with a sparker gang known as the “Car Kids”. Through the course of the song, it talks about their struggles, and their eventual capturing, leaving Mylo emotionally unstable since the witnessing, and his parents to rot in jail.

description.plain:
“Lovers in Japan” is the fifth track and third single of Viva la Vida. On the LP this track is coupled to “Reign of Love.”

In an interview for Entertainment Weekly in 2008, lead singer Chris Martin, when talking about the song and its title, remarked that “No one associates romance with Japan…Everyone thinks Japan is just about Hitachi and neon signs, but every time we’re there, we see these amazing sunrises. It’s very sexy.”

A slightly uptempo version of this song (the “Osaka Sun Mix”) appeared on Prospekt’s March.

An acoustic version also appeared as an iTunes pre-order bonus track.

description.plain:
“A Message” is a love song and the eighth track of Coldplay’s X&Y. The lyrics and melody were inspired by John Ireland’s 1664 hymn “My Song Is Love Unknown,” which is also Chris Martin’s favorite hymn.

Around the time that Coldplay was recording X&Y, Chris Martin’s father-in-law passed away. “A Message” may have been written for his wife Gwyneth Paltrow, who reportedly (and understandably) went into a depression after her father’s death (Martin supposedly wrote “Fix You” as a way of cheering her up).

description.plain: “The Hardest Part” is about the ending of a long and loving relationship, and the feelings that are left behind when the person is gone. The lyrics talk about the sorrowful and painful feelings and memories that remain when somebody you loved leaves your life. Chris is confused and tries to work out what went wrong (similar to The Scientist), and in the 3rd verse it all collapses in a storm of sadness and self-loathing.

description.plain:
“Flags,” a bonus track included in the Japanese version of the album, points out how borders and flags can’t divide people since they are all from the same essence and soul. The song refers to every person individually, free from their geographical differences and sexual preferences.

One year after its release, the song was released worldwide on December 21, 2020, with the band stating that they love the song, but did not have space for it on the standard tracklist of Everyday Life.

description.plain:
Official soundtrack for Angelina Jolie’s movie as director “Unbroken”, premiered on December 25th, 2014.



The band, whose leader Chris Martin identifies himself religiously as “alltheist”, wrote the song by basing on the movie’s story: its main character is the American runner and Olympic athlete Louis Zamperini, who got captured by Japanese armies in 1943, during the battles of World War II in the Pacific Ocean, and sent to a prison camp for two years, throughout those “The Bird”, a Japanese sergeant, constantly beat Louis in a psychotic fury.

After his liberation, in 1949, in an effort to get over his trauma, Zamperini took part, together with his wife, to the Los Angeles Crusade, a campaign by the evangelist Billy Graham: the experience made the former athlete convert to Christianity and taught him the power of forgiveness and love, so he could have mercy on his persecutors.
As Louis wrote on his autobiography, “Devil at My Heels:”

I think the hardest thing in life is to forgive. Hate is self-destructive. If you hate someone, you’re not hurting the person you hate, you’re hurting yourself.

description.plain:
“Glass Of Water” is a song featured on Coldplay’s Prospekt’s March EP from 2008.

It was originally a song written during sessions for Coldplay’s fourth album, but didn’t make it onto the album’s final tracklisting. However, the song features heavily in the booklet of Viva La Vida Or Death And All His Friends despite being cut from the album.

The title appears on the big painting in the booklet’s centrefold, above some of the song’s lyrics, and the very first page of the album is a map of Brazil with more lyrics from Glass Of Water scribbled over it in crayon. However, the song’s lyrics have drastically changed since the painting was made.



  


In the chorus, the song shifts into an unusual 7/4 time signature, making it one of the band’s most complex songs. In general many of them were written during the VLVODAOHF era.

description.plain:
During the Manchester benefit concert One Love, Chris Martin and Jonny Buckland performed an acoustic cover of Oasis' 1995 anthem “Don’t Look Back In Anger”. He prefaced it by thanking Ariana Grande for hosting the concert and saying it was Britain’s turn to sing for her.



The song became representative of the defiant hopeful spirit of the city of Manchester in the wake of the bombings that happened at Ariana’s Dangerous Woman show on May 22. During the city’s vigil in the following days, a crowd spontaneously sang it during the one minute’s silence.

description.plain:
With the first part being a slow piano medley, and vocal samples, and the second incorporating a faster tempo and rock instruments, Up with the Birds is the grand finale to Coldplay’s modern-day rock opera Mylo Xyloto, departing with a sad and happy tone. With grandiose emphasis, and underestimated vocals by Chris Martin, Up with the Birds ensures safety and protection to the people of Silencia, including Fly, as critics generally well-received the limited-edition single for being a perfect closer to the album.



Mylo dies after sustaining fatal injuries, as he knows that he has departed to Heaven, due to his faith in God, and the battle is over. The winner is the rebels and he is not there, as everyone mourns him, and he accepts new life. But he knows, from God, that good times will soon come, and everyone will be happy, and that when danger comes, everyone will fight back to ensure democracy and freedom.

description.plain:
Electronica meets graffiti, in this wondrous opener to Coldplay’s modern-day rock opera, “Mylo Xyloto”. A ‘70s synth, echoing guitars, and global instruments, as well as a tinkling glockenspiel help put the album on the path to a spectacle of a land filled, with war, colour, crime, love, fascism, martial rule, and hope.

The song serves as a prologue to the album, and opens up the listener to the plot, much like the gateway to Neverland, the “second star to the right, and straight on till morning”.

description.plain:
The stripped-down version of “Everglow” was released on 11 November 2016 as the fifth single overall from the group’s seventh studio album. This newly-recorded remix is an acoustic version of the original song included in the album.

This remix is inspired by Chris' unrehearsed solo performance of the song at the 2016 Glastonbury Festival due to a technical mishap. This acoustic version removes Gwyneth Paltrow’s vocals and instead ended with a sample of Muhammad Ali’s 1977 speech in Newcastle upon Tyne, UK.

This remix was featured on Coldplay’s A Head Full of Dreams Tour setlist, starting from Leg 3.

Here’s a performance of this song recorded in Australia.

description.plain: Originally on the Japanese version of Coldplay’s ‘debut’ album Parachutes, For You was released as a bonus track along with Careful Where You Stand. It is also one of the least known Coldplay songs. This spacey, slow and chilled out song is about friends and peers worrying about an individual. This track captures and foreshadows what the group would be doing in their 3rd studio album X & Y. Instead of the loud, raw alternative-pop sound Coldplay had from their beginning of their careers.

[Liam Neeson narration]
In an exclusive Red Nose Day revelation, we've discovered that the British band, Coldplay, are secretly working on a musical of TV sensation, Game of Thrones.

(guitar and vocals)
♪ Bom, bom, bom  baba dobodom ♪

Wait, wait, how many poppadoms?

[Narration]
The band had been long-time fans of the show, and bearded drummer, Will Champion, actually took time off at one point to act in the famous 'Red Wedding' episode.
They've gathered in the Henson recording studio in Los Angeles to work up the 16 songs required for a full Broadway stage production.

(keyboard)
[Will Champion]
- Nice! Have you got any lyrics?
[Chris Martin]
- Yeah.
[Chris Martin singing "Closer to Home"]
♪ Around the world my heart had to roam ♪

[Chris Martin - continued]

(music continues as female voiceover begins)

[Chris Martin - singing]
♪ Closer to home ♪
(band plays 'Red Wedding instrumental')
(piano music)
Cut to: RAK Studios, London

Finally, after months of writing and planning, Chris has invited along the entire cast of Game of Thrones, to recruit them into the live Broadway show.

[Chris Martin]
Fella's, how ya doin'?

[Chris Martin]
I had a moment of inspiration, it was
a flash of genius -- get the whole cast to come in. Everyone thought it was a brilliant idea, so that's what's happening. It's a big day, big day for us.

[Camera pans, the chairs are empty..]
Well, not all of them.
[... outside of Iwan Rheoon and Mark Addy.]
More ... two.

I was told Sean Bean was gonna be here. He owes me a fiver.

This is called "Rastafarian Targaryen."

♪ I'mma Rastafarian Targaryen ♪
♪ I got some dragons and they're
pretty scary-en ♪

(interviewer)
So Chris, how you think it's going?
[Chris Martin]
Stunning. Stunning.  People are literally stunned.
(interviewer)
And what if some of them can't sing?
[Chris Martin]
Well, the funny thing is, they can sing.

[Chris Martin]
A two, three, four!
[Cut to the band playing "Red Wedding" while Ewan and Mark sing along]
♪ Bom, bom, bom baba
(Chris Martin)
Robert.... Robert! Snappy! Come on.
[Mark Addy]
No, no, I-sorry, sorry.
[Jonny Buckland]
I'm sure he'll come back.
[Chris Martin]
Well, with these things it's always step by step. Um, 50% of the cast seemed really into it, so, um... I think we're onto something really special.

(piano)

It's been a slightly disappointing day. But then...
[Kit Harrington]
Hey Chris. I'm sorry I'm late.
[Chris Martin]
Oh my god. Jon Snow. I knew you'd come.
[Kit Harington]
I'd never let you down, man.

It's Kit.

[John Bradley]

Oh, lovely!
[Thomas Brodie-Sangster ]

description.plain:
A hidden message beyond that of human capability, “M.M.I.X” delivers a 1 minute intermission to get ready for the upcoming horrors of the government; mentally, physically, violently, grisly, and remorsefully. Synths, samples, and electronica are all filling the air up, with the song a cupcake, and the instruments being the frosting of the sixth track.

A message hidden, the lyrics are only said in the booklet, with song being instrumental, making this one of the album’s most interesting and controversial songs. The lyrics describe Mylo having a conversation for the first time with the rebel leader, Fly, and the possible outcomes of the rebels being deported.

description.plain:
Through a Billboard interview with  Kygo called Kygo Talks Mixing for Diplo, Coldplay and Upcoming Tour he talked about this and another songs:

Music producer Kygo put his inimitably chill spin on Midnight, the vocoder-heavy electronic single from Coldplay.

While a lesser artist might shirk at the thought of having to follow the legendary Giorgio Moroder with a remix of the same song Midnight: Giorgio Moroder Remix, Kygo certainly gives the father of modern dance music take on Coldplay’s brooding single. Furthermore, this is one of  Kygo’s first official (non-bootleg) remixes–and considering it’s one of the world’s most popular rock bands, it’s safe to say the young Norwegian is on to something.

Kygo’s Midnight remix was broadcast from the premiere on Pete Tong’s BBC Radio 1 show in 2014. The original Midnight mix comes from Coldplay’s LP, Ghost Stories.

description.plain:
1st song on Safety EP, May 1998 and The Blue Room EP, October 1999.

This song sarcastically represents the insatiable desire of humans to continually create and have bigger, better things, ways of doing things, and overall lifestyles, even when these such things are already at a reasonable standard.

An interesting observation involving this song and the EP’s closer, “Such A Rush”, is that they both touch on the idea of humans constantly pursuing materialistic lifestyles, but this song does so through the sarcastic view of the narrator themself wishing to have a better life, while “Such A Rush” explicitly mentions the money-centric desires of humans to the audience. This is a particular way to address an issue in the sequencing of albums, where both the opening and closing tracks make reference to the same idea/s, and in this case, the message is portrayed in different ways to deliver a message.

description.plain:
This version of “Talk” comes as the result of the band’s frustrations in the production of the X&Y, having at the time scrapped what would eventually be released on the final tracklist, in a last minute decision. An interesting note is that this version was recorded after the album version but was scrapped.

This version was leaked onto the internet in early 2005 when Will Champion sent an email containing the file to the wrong recipient, amidst immense pressure from the record label and the band itself.

description.plain:
“Crests Of Waves” is the second song on Coldplay’s Clocks EP.  It’s one of two otherwise unreleased songs on the EP; the other is called  “Animals”.

Lyrically, “Crests of Waves” compares love to an ocean.  It’s a classic metaphor, one which Juliet uses in Shakespeare’s most-famous play:

And yet I wish but for the thing I have:
My bounty is as boundless as the sea,
My love as deep; the more I give to thee,
The more I have, for both are infinite.

In Coldplay’s telling, the ebbs and flows of love appear like cresting waves.

songs.lyrics:
[Spoken]
This being human is a guest house
Every morning, a new arrival
A joy, a depression, a meanness
Some momentary awareness comes
As an unexpected visitor
Welcome and entertain them all
Even if they are a crowd of sorrows
Who violently sweep your house empty of its furniture
Still, treat each guest honorably
He may be clearing you out for some new delight
The dark thought, the shame, the malice
Meet them at the door laughing and invite them in
Be grateful for whoever comes
Because each has been sent as a guide from beyond

description.plain:
A leftover from the band’s sessions with Ken Nelson, which ended in turmoil after dissatisfaction with the sound and creative direction.

“The World Turned Upside Down” shares the title with a song oftenly played on A Rush of Blood to the Head tour, as Will Champion said on the band’s official e-zine, “some old song titles have been given to new songs, so there might be some familiar bits and bobs in there.”

description.plain:
The single version of “Lovers in Japan” is exactly the same as the album version, but it’s missing the “Reign of Love” hidden song that appears on Viva La Vida or Death and All His Friends. It was first released as a promotional single for the album, but this version later appeared on 2009’s Prospekt’s March EP.

It didn’t quite make the Billboard Hot 100, but it’s still one of Coldplay’s most popular songs and remains a live favourite.

description.plain: “Don Quixote” is a song Coldplay performed while on tour in South America in 2010. Though it never appeared on an actual album, and there was never a studio recording of it, it remained popular with fans and elements of the song have been incorporated into future Coldplay songs like “Hurts Like Heaven” and “Ink”.

description.plain: Brothers & Sisters" is a song by Coldplay, released as their first single in 1999 following the release of the band’s first EP Safety, released a year earlier. It was later re-released as an EP. The song has peaked at number 92 on the UK Singles Chart. The EP includes “Easy To Please” and “Only Superstition.”

description.plain:
“Death Will Never Conquer” was performed acoustically during the Viva la Vida tour, with drummer Will Champion taking lead on vocals and Chris Martin playing harmonica.

A studio version with Chris at the piano was later released as a free download on Coldplay’s website, served as the B-side for the “Viva la Vida” single and was a bonus track on the Japan release of the LP.

description.plain:
“Houston #1” is a song made about the city of Houston. Coldplay were going to play a show at the NRG Stadium on 8/25/17, but due to Hurricane Harvey, they couldn’t, to insure the safety of everyone.

The song was played in Miami on 8/29/17 live on the C-stage and will only be played once, stated by the band’s front-man, Chris Martin.

“Houston #1” takes a country centric taste, describing the city of Houston in distraught from Hurricane Harvey, being told to just keep on keeping on.

description.plain:
“Lhuna” is a charity single performed by the British band Coldplay and Australian singer-songwriter Kylie Minogue.

It was recorded during the sessions of Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends, but never made on the final cut. When asked why the song did not appear on the album, Chris Martin said that it was too “sexy”. Afterwards, the song was expected to appear on the Prospekt’s March EP, but did not make it. Finally, it was released as a charity single on 1 December 2008 to promote World AIDS Day.

When asked why the song did not appear on the album, Chris Martin said that it was too “sexy”. Afterwards, the song was expected to appear on the Prospekt’s March EP, but did not make it. Finally, it was released as a charity single on 1 December 2008 to promote World AIDS Day.

description.plain:
Rolling Stone describe the song remix through an article called Dance Legend Giorgio Moroder Gives Coldplay’s ‘Midnight’ a Disco Remix

One of Coldplay’s most unassuming tracks off their forthcoming record Ghost Stories is now its most danceable. Electronic music pioneer Giorgio Moroder, who has collaborated with Donna Summer, Blondie and Daft Punk, has shined his disco ball on the pop-rockers' EDM-leaning, chill-out cut “Midnight”, which the group debuted in February.

While the original track bowed out after five minutes, Moroder has turned it into a lengthier, harder-hitting eight-minute affair with no time squandered. He adds a pounding bass-drum beat from the onset and then uses the synth filigrees toward the end of the track – the part of the song’s video that goes from black and white to stop-motion color so (presumably) Chris Martin can wave his arms to the music – to build it into something that would have once backed Summer. Vocal “aahs” and soft pads of synths, alongside robotic chanting in French, make the track more Moroder than Martin for the final four minutes.

body.plain:
Coldplay likes to cover this James Bond theme on stage, as captured here on record at Rockefeller Music Hall, Oslo, Norway, on 1st of December, 2000 for the standard “Don’t Panic” single release.

This along with “Bigger Stronger” were the two missing songs that completed their setlist from the live concert, the remaining appearing in their Norwegian Live EP.

description.plain:
A demo from the Viva era, leaked July 2009, this piano-oriented song tells a tale, with words being inspired by the French Revolution as was Viva La Vida or Death and All His Friends.

It is the only demo from this era to have been played live beforehand, as Chris Martin performed it for a charity event in November 2006, at Mencap Little Noise Sessions.

description.plain:
“Lukas” was originally planned for Viva La Vida or Death and All His Friends, but got scrapped from the final set of tracks. Coldplay gifted the song to Natalie Imbruglia, who would release the song in 2009.

Around early 2011, a studio recording was leaked, alongside other unreleased material from the Viva La Vida sessions, labeled as an instrumental, however Chris Martin’s vocals can still be heard quietly from the guitar microphones.

description.plain:
Initially planned for X&Y, the song was scrapped in the band’s sessions with Ken Nelson, who had produced the first two albums.

The band played this version of the track on A Rush of Blood to the Head’s tour, with the lyrics being slightly altered from show to show.

Shares the title with Fix You’s b-side, as Will Champion said on the band’s official e-zine, “some old song titles have been given to new songs, so there might be some familiar bits and bobs in there.”

The fans, to distinguish both versions easier, have named this one “Your World Turned Upside Down” and “The World Turns Upside Down”.

description.plain:
One of the much lesser known songs in the band’s double decade-spanning catalogue, only one version of “Pour Me” has ever been officially released: a live version (recorded at the Hollywood Bowl in 2003) as a b-side on the single release for “Fix You”. It was exclusively played in 2003 on the A Rush of Blood to the Head Tour as a song intended for later release during the band’s third album era.

The lyrics of this song may come off as a bit confusing, especially when the song title is taken into consideration, since “poor” and “pour” are homophones.. The title “Pour Me” doesn’t literally make sense, and the official lyric of “Poor me” seems to be a much more fitting one. The band have never explained the title, and some even speculate that it is possibly a play on “poor”, a reference to the self-pitying nature of the lyrics, and the French “pour”, to mean “for me”.

description.plain:
“Wedding Bells” started being written in the Viva La Vida era, when the band started preparing for the follow-up album. On The South Bank Show’s documentary about the 2008 album, Chris plays an early sketch of the song:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hP8NsRgfP4U

The song got played live once before transforming into “Christmas Lights”. Chris Martin played “Wedding Bells” one last time in a solo gig in April 2011.

description.plain:
On the Coldplaying forum, user NOWAYME found that there’s proof within the master of the track “Talk” that the lyrics were changed at last minute.

By looking at the spectogram, the producer placed in the new lines on a rush and didn’t adjust the vocal track for a homogeneous sound.



What’s more, the original lyrics are featured on all of the official remixes with varied vocal takes from different sessions of the band, with a persistent verse structure.

description.plain:
Originally planned for the X&Y album but got scrapped in early sessions. The song was revived after the band got done with their 2007 tour, as it shows in the A Head Full of Dreams documentary film, for the following album Viva La Vida or Death and All His Friends, but once again getting left over in the process.

Around early 2011, a studio recording was leaked, alongside other unreleased material from the Viva La Vida sessions, labeled as an instrumental, as Chris' vocals can only be heard from the piano microphones.

description.plain:
While pursuing a major record label to sign to, the group’s manager and friend Phil Harvey released a demo tape to various labels that included two songs: “Ode to Deodorant” and “Brothers + Sisters”.

The group would re-work this song in their single release under their first record label Fierce Panda Records, then re-work the song again as a B-side under their second record label Parlophone.
